extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for Nature Portfolio journals (and prospective reviewers/editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy for assessing manuscripts submitted to Nature Portfolio journals, including what to evaluate in reports, procedural expectations (confidentiality, timing, anonymity), and journal-level publication criteria. Intended to direct reviewers on how to prepare reports that assist editors and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of contributions subject to peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists the contribution types that are peer-reviewed by Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The following types of contribution are peer-reviewed: Articles, Letters, Brief Communications, Matters Arising, Technical Reports, Analysis, Resources, Reviews, Perspectives and Insight articles. Correspondence and published corrections may also be peer-reviewed at the editor's discretion. Other contributed articles are not usually peer-reviewed but may be at editors' discretion, especially if they present technical information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper should represent an advance in understanding likely to influence thinking in the field, with strong evidence for its conclusions, and there should be a discernible reason it deserves Nature Portfolio visibility rather than a specialist journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether the manuscript is sufficiently novel and of broad interest. Strong evidence must support conclusions. Consider whether the work merits the higher visibility of a Nature Portfolio journal compared with specialist journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial pre-screening and suitability for external review
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors read all submitted manuscripts and send for formal review only those most likely to meet editorial criteria; others are promptly rejected without external review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts judged insufficient in general interest or otherwise inappropriate may be rejected without external review. Editors may use informal advice from specialists when making these pre-screening decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose of the reviewer report
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the editors with the information needed to reach a decision and instruct authors how to strengthen their paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should inform editorial decisions and also guide authors on revisions. Negative reviews should explain the major weaknesses so rejected authors can understand reasons and how to improve for other journals. Confidential comments to the editor are allowed but should not contradict the main points addressed to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise what you consider to be the outstanding features of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary of the manuscript's main contributions and standout findings to help editors quickly grasp the paper's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manuscript have flaws which should prohibit its publication? Provide details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify fatal technical or interpretational flaws. Give specific reasons and evidence for any assertion that the work is invalid or contains errors that preclude publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the conclusions are not original, provide relevant references. Subjectively assess whether results are of immediate interest to many in the discipline and/or to people across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on novelty, situate the work in the literature, and indicate the breadth of interest. Provide citations to prior work if originality is in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data & methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the validity of the approach, quality of the data and quality of presentation. Review all data, including extended data and supplementary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether methods are appropriate and sufficiently described for replication. Note any issues in data quality, availability, or presentation across main and supplementary files. State if reporting is detailed and transparent enough to reproduce results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of statistics and treatment of uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: All error bars should be defined in the corresponding figure legends; comment on the appropriateness of statistical tests and accuracy of descriptions of error bars and probability values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check statistical methods, definitions of error bars, p-values/uncertainty reporting, and appropriateness of tests. Provide specific critique or confirmation of correct usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the conclusions and data interpretation are robust, valid and reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate if conclusions are supported by data and analyses. Flag overinterpretation or unwarranted extrapolation, and indicate where interpretations are or are not justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: List additional experiments or data that could help strengthen the work in a revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, prioritized suggestions for experiments, analyses or clarifications that would materially improve the manuscript and address key weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: References
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the manuscript references previous literature appropriately; suggest inclusions or exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify missing key citations, or point out unnecessary references. Provide specific references that should be added or removed, with brief justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the abstract clear and accessible? Are abstract, introduction and conclusions appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate readability and contextualisation for the target audience. Recommend changes to improve clarity, narrative flow, and how the work is framed in the introduction and conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflammatory material
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manuscript contain any language that is inappropriate or potentially libelous?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag wording that could be defamatory or otherwise inappropriate. Recommend neutral, factual phrasing where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity and inclusion concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise any concerns that may in your view have an impact on diversity, equity and inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out issues (e.g., sampling bias, exclusionary language/methods) that could affect fairness or generalizability across demographic groups and suggest remedies if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of expertise / parts outside expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate any part of the manuscript, data, or analyses that you feel is outside the scope of your expertise, or that you were unable to assess fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about limitations of your review and state which aspects should be evaluated by additional specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address editor's specific questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer any other specific question asked by the editor via email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond directly to tailored editorial queries, and flag if you cannot assess certain items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify statements and document thought process
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should document the referees’ thought process. All statements should be justified and argued in detail, naming facts and citing supporting references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unsupported assertions; provide line-item evidence, references, and reasoning for criticisms and endorsements. The order of items can vary, but completeness and justification are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline-specific standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all of the recommended aspects will apply to every paper due to discipline-specific standards; when in doubt contact the editor for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt evaluation to field norms; consult the editor when unclear about applicable disciplinary expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality on jurisdictional claims in maps and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is policy to remain neutral with respect to jurisdictional claims in published maps and institutional affiliations; naming conventions are left to authors' discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should not request changes to place names or affiliations unless critical to the scientific clarity of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use by peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not upload manuscripts into generative AI tools; if any part of the evaluation was supported by an AI tool, the reviewer must declare its use transparently in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because generative AI can be inaccurate and may expose confidential material, reviewers should avoid using such tools on manuscript text; transparency is required if any AI assistance was used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to respond promptly within the number of days agreed and to inform the editor if they anticipate a longer delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely communication allows editors to keep authors informed or find alternate reviewers; honour the agreed deadline or notify the editor early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity policy for referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees' identities are not released to authors or other reviewers unless a referee voluntarily signs their comments. Reviewers are asked not to identify themselves to authors while the manuscript is under consideration without the editor's knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If choosing to sign, consider that reports and identities may be shared among reviewers and transferred journals; signing may make later interactions more challenging. The journal will not confirm or deny speculation about reviewer identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymized peer review option
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Nature-branded journals and Communications journals offer a double-anonymized peer review option where authors remain anonymous to referees; authors are responsible for anonymizing their manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors choosing this option must follow an anonymization checklist provided by the journal. Reviewers should consult the specific journal website for application details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review option
rubrics_metrics.description: Several Nature journals publish details about the peer-review process (reviewer comments, author rebuttals, and sometimes editorial decision letters) as part of the publication; authors are offered the opportunity to opt in at completion of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If opted in, a peer review file is published but will not contain all information considered in editorial decisions (e.g., editor discussions or confidential comments). Policies vary by journal; check journal-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing referees' reports
rubrics_metrics.description: As a matter of policy, editors do not suppress reviewers' reports; they may edit to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information about other matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should avoid needless offence but are encouraged to state their opinion plainly. Editors will transmit comments intended for authors except in rare cases where editing for offensiveness or confidentiality is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors select referees based on many factors, including expertise, reputation, specific recommendations and previous experience; they prefer referees who are quick, careful and provide reasoning for their views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity, equity and inclusion are considered in reviewer selection; authors may suggest reviewers or request exclusions, which the editor will sympathetically consider but not be bound by.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to necessary literature
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer lacks access to any published paper necessary for evaluation, the journal will supply a copy upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send publication references of required papers to the handling editor; the editor will obtain the paper and pay any necessary fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the peer-review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors, authors and reviewers must keep confidential all details of the editorial and peer review process on submitted manuscripts unless part of open peer review; correspondence, referees' reports and other confidential material must not be published or disclosed without prior written consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer seeks advice from colleagues, they must consult the editor and ensure confidentiality is maintained; names of consulted colleagues must be provided to the journal with the final report. Note that reviewer anonymity cannot be guaranteed in the face of successful legal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct reporting and potential contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio reserves the right to contact funders, regulatory bodies, journals and the authors’ institutions in cases of suspected research or publishing misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may escalate concerns about misconduct and involve appropriate external bodies; reviewers should flag such concerns to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, security and seeking additional advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may seek advice on ethical issues, data or materials access, or societal/security implications of publishing a paper, usually simultaneously with technical peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should raise ethical, data access or security concerns in their reports; final publication decisions remain the responsibility of the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to review revisions / follow-up advice
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers agree to assess a paper, this is considered a commitment to review subsequent revisions; reviewers should be willing to provide follow-up advice when asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may not send a resubmitted paper back to reviewers if authors have not seriously attempted to address criticisms. Reviewers will sometimes be reconsulted to resolve disagreements or clarify points.
